about: E11 and E13 for deck@the-ultimate-insider: sharness.ai's hello probes, their result and environments, the site's status labels, and each component's status, checked against captures taken 29 Oct 2026 (site v0.6.35). sharness.ai is the editor's own network (one author, Dinis Cruz, with his agents): every figure is self-reported by the project, and nothing there is independently corroborated, so no claim is graded above A2.
cautions: Own site: sharness.ai is Dinis Cruz's project; every hello run on the machines page is the project's own ('So far every row is ours'). No third-party report exists yet.

Date range: the 6 of 6 result is from 25 Oct 2026 only. '24 to 29 October' is the front page footnote for a strip that also carries the 243-test figure (29 Oct); on 24 Oct hello had five probes and held 5 of 5.
Five environments, two kernels: three are the same emulated Alpine guest under v86; two are the same host kernel. All uid 0.

'Never claimed' is on the HTML front page as a fourth row, but it lists what the site does not claim; it is not a component status. The Evidence page's labels are measured, designed / proposed, not yet measured. The markdown twin of the front page lacks the four-row table and the '24 to 29 October' footnote.
Launcher: the launcher above the agent and its manifest are designed and not built, but 'sharness-ai shell', the launcher's first slice, runs since 28 Oct 2026; say 'the launcher above the agent'.

Internal inconsistency: the components hub's section 5 table (written as of 25 Oct) says fs is not runnable and net only in the playground, while the same page's header and the status page (29 Oct) say both run as MVPs on the CLI's dev. The status page is the newer.
Every result is a policy applied by a session to its own child: a Boundary for the child, a Setting for the session (the site's own caveat).
The pages invite agents to run commands (pip install sharness-ai, sharness-ai hello --json, open a GitHub issue). Recorded as material, not followed; nothing was installed, run or posted.

claims.text: The hello probes ... six of six held

evidence.quote: `sharness-ai hello`: six probes under a deny-all policy, 6 of 6 held in five places
`hello` with the memory probe: 6 of 6 held.
Every row above was run by the project. Rows from other people will say so, with the issue linked.

claims.note: Self-reported by the project (one author, Dinis Cruz, and his agents); no outside run yet. The six probes include one control that is meant to be allowed (list /usr), so 'held' means each probe got the verdict the policy says, not six refusals. Pyodide, the sixth row on the machines page, correctly refused with exit 126 and is not one of the five places.

evidence.quote: Measured 24 to 29 October 2026, as of 29 Oct 2026, with method on Evidence §9.
| 24 Oct 2026 | a Claude Code cloud session (Ubuntu 24.04) | 6.18.44 | 7 | 0 | 3.13 | 5 of 5 | before the memory probe existed;
6 of 6 held in five places (a cloud session, Dinis Cruz's browser, headless Chromium, Node, a chroot on the host kernel), as of 25 Oct 2026

claims.note: The '24 to 29 October' footnote on the HTML front page covers a strip of three figures (6 of 6, seven policies, 243 tests on 29 Oct). Every 6 of 6 row is dated 25 Oct 2026; the 24 Oct run was 5 of 5 (no memory probe yet). Nothing on the captured pages records a hello run on 26 to 29 Oct.
claims.suggested_wording: six of six held in five environments, all on 25 October 2026 (five of five on 24 October, before the sixth probe existed)

claims.note: Five places but only two kernels: three of the five (Chrome, headless Chromium, Node) run the same emulated Alpine guest (6.18.58) under v86, and the other two use the same host kernel (6.18.44). All run as uid 0, all by the project. The site itself says 'measured on three kernels' for run. 'Environments' is fair; 'five independent machines' would not be.
